stem: Monthly cost reports show unexpected charges from a full EBS volume and a full FSx file system, both of which needed manual capacity increases. Select TWO storage layers whose capacity has to be requested or automated explicitly, because they do not grow unattended on their own. (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Amazon S3 buckets using a Lifecycle policy

rationale: Amazon EBS volumes stay at their provisioned size until resized, so their capacity increases have to be requested or automated explicitly. Amazon FSx file systems also need capacity increases requested explicitly on most deployment types, matching the pattern in the report. Amazon S3 buckets scale storage capacity automatically with nothing to provision, so they never hit this problem. Amazon EFS file systems similarly grow and shrink with usage automatically. Applying a Lifecycle policy to an S3 bucket changes which storage class holds aging objects; it does not change that S3 capacity already scales on its own.
